paper.title: MetaMem: Evolving Meta-Memory for Knowledge Utilization through Self-Reflective Symbolic Optimization
paper.central_claim: A self-evolving meta-memory of knowledge-utilization experiences, learned by self-reflection and ADD/DEL/MOD edits against ground-truth correctness, improves LLM use of memorized knowledge on LongMemEval (over 3.6% above strong baselines) and generalizes across memory systems and construction domains.

missing_sections: Figures 3-6 are images (values not in text)

evidence.quote: aiming to teach LLMs how to effectively utilize memorized knowledge.
evidence.support_explanation: Retained object is a self-evolving meta-memory of knowledge-utilization experience, separate from the factual memory (built by LightMem).

evidence.quote: the resulting memory units are often fragmented or even contradictory
evidence.support_explanation: Author gap: construction-side memory systems yield fragmented/contradictory units that LLMs misuse; the case study (Appendix A.8) is qualitative.

evidence.quote: This operation is designed to eliminate obsolete or erroneous experience units.
evidence.support_explanation: Deletion exists as one of three LLM-chosen edit actions (ADD/DEL/MOD).

evidence.quote: Since actions proposed by different instances may conflict, we further apply a filtering instruction,
evidence.support_explanation: Per-instance LLM edit proposals are merged by an LLM conflict-filter; no measured-utility acceptance test appears.

evidence.quote: We then employ a stronger model as a judge to evaluate each sampled response
evidence.support_explanation: Feedback signal = ground-truth correctness assessed by a stronger LLM judge (Qwen3-235B), then self-reflection on each response.

evidence.quote: we initialize the meta-memory as an empty state
evidence.support_explanation: Meta-memory starts empty and is updated batch by batch (no privileged seeding).

evidence.quote: we employ 5-fold cross-validation for evaluation, where each fold allocates 400 samples for Meta-Memory construction and 100 samples for testing.
evidence.support_explanation: Held-out protocol: 5 folds over 500 LongMemEval questions; test fold disjoint from construction questions.

evidence.quote: For each fold, a subset of 100 samples is reserved as the independent test set, while the remaining data is partitioned into 350 samples for meta-memory training and 50 samples for validation.
evidence.support_explanation: A 50-sample validation split exists but its use (checkpoint choice, early stopping, accept/reject of edits) is not described.

evidence.quote: We reported the final results by calculating the average performance across these five folds.
evidence.support_explanation: Headline numbers average five fold test sets; fold-level table (Table 5) is provided.
MetaMem Qwen average 71.90; Single-Assistant column only 38.14.
Strongest baseline LightMem: 67.50 average.
RAG scores 88.37 on Single-Assistant versus MetaMem 38.14: the meta-memory/LightMem stack is far worse on that category.
Ablation w/o Evolution 68.33 vs full 71.90 (+3.57) and w/o Self-Reflection 70.02; LightMem baseline is 67.50, so w/o Evolution is not equal to the no-meta-memory baseline.

evidence.quote: MetaMem w/o Evolution, which disables the evolution of the meta-memory
evidence.support_explanation: Definition of the key ablation is one clause; what meta-memory content (if any) remains is not specified.

evidence.quote: compared with MetaMem w/o Evolution, MetaMem achieves more than 3% performance improvements
evidence.support_explanation: Author-reported effect of iterative optimization.
Toggling the learned meta-memory on a different system: Full Text 51.50 -> 53.25 (Qwen); RAG 62.25 -> 66.42 (next rows); Temporal Reasoning drops for Full Text.
Fold-level results: MetaMem beats LightMem on all 5 Qwen folds and 4 of 5 Llama folds (our reading of Table 5).
One of ten fold-by-backbone comparisons is a loss (63.6 vs 66.7); gives a failure count that the main table hides.

evidence.quote: performance on most tasks begins to decline after peaking at step 5
evidence.support_explanation: Over-training degrades the store: accuracy peaks around step 5 then declines.

evidence.quote: the accuracy peaks at step 5 and subsequently exhibits a downward trend
evidence.support_explanation: Unit count keeps rising (~25-27 units) while accuracy falls; no rollback to the best checkpoint is described and which step is reported in Table 1 is unspecified.

evidence.quote: MetaMem w/ Qwen3-235B-A22B Judge 71.9 MetaMem w/ Qwen3-30B-A3B-Instruct Judge 72.1 MetaMem w/ Llama3.1-70B-Instruct Judge 71.6
evidence.support_explanation: Judge-model sensitivity: 71.6-72.1 across three judges, all above LightMem 67.5.

evidence.quote: randomly sample 1,000 instances with a random seed of 42
evidence.support_explanation: Out-of-domain construction corpus (ShareGPT, 1,000 conversations, seed 42); numbers for MetaMem(ShareGPT) are in Figure 3 only.

evidence.quote: both MetaMem (ShareGPT) and MetaMem (LongMemEval) consistently outperform the baseline LightMem model
evidence.support_explanation: Cross-domain evidence: meta-memory built from ShareGPT also beats LightMem on LongMemEval (figure-only values).

evidence.quote: The model is trained for 5 epochs with a batch size of 50.
evidence.support_explanation: Construction budget in epochs/batch only; judge/reflection/action/filter calls and GPU time not given.

evidence.quote: performing 5 samples per instance
evidence.support_explanation: Five sampled responses per training instance, each judged and reflected on by LLMs: the main construction cost driver.

evidence.quote: MetaMem incurs negligible overhead due to the encoding of additional meta-directives
evidence.support_explanation: Inference tokens/latency are reported (Table 4); construction cost is stated to be offline and unreported.

evidence.quote: relies on an LLM-based judgment model to evaluate complex human-LLM interactions during meta-memory construction
evidence.support_explanation: Authors flag judge dependence; in-domain training outperforms out-of-domain.

evidence.quote: For a fair comparison, all methods employ the same backbone LLM and retriever in our experiments.
evidence.support_explanation: Matched backbone and retriever across baselines (not matched for construction compute).

evidence.quote: the effectiveness of MetaMem is decoupled from the underlying memory system
evidence.support_explanation: Authors claim decoupling from the memory substrate based on Full Text and RAG variants only.

evidence.quote: Qwen3-235B-A22B Yang et al. (2025) for response judgment
evidence.support_explanation: A single 235B model judges responses during construction; Table 6 varies it.

evidence.quote: General units increases steadily from approximately 65% to over 80%
evidence.support_explanation: Generalization of units is measured by an LLM classifier (GLM-4.5), not by transfer tests.

evidence.quote: eventually widening the performance gap to 2.9% at 1,000 samples
evidence.support_explanation: Data-scaling on ShareGPT-built meta-memory; below 400 samples MetaMem slightly underperforms; gap 2.9 at 1,000.

evidence.quote: Single-Session User 70 Single-Session Assistant 56 Multi-Session 133 Temporal Reasoning 133 Knowledge Update 78 Single-Session Preference 30
evidence.support_explanation: Category sizes over 500 questions; a fold test has 100 questions (about 6 Preference items), so per-category fold numbers are very coarse.

Our arithmetic: Qwen fold averages LightMem 67.7/68.7/69.7/60.6/62.6 (mean 65.9) vs Table 1 LightMem 67.50; MetaMem 70.7/77.8/75.8/70.7/64.6 (mean 71.9 matches). Llama LightMem fold mean 66.1 matches Table 1 66.17. So the Qwen baseline row is not on the same five test folds.

evidence.quote: Extensive experiments demonstrate the effectiveness of MetaMem, which significantly outperforms strong baselines by over 3.6%.
evidence.support_explanation: Headline claim; our check: absolute margins over LightMem are +4.40 (Qwen) and +2.91 (Llama), whose mean 3.65 equals the headline.
MetaMem Llama average 69.08 vs LightMem 66.17 (+2.91).

signatures.object: meta-memory: a short list (about 25-27 units at the end) of natural-language knowledge-utilization experience units injected into every query prompt alongside retrieved memory fragments; the factual memory (LightMem) is not edited
signatures.information: training: question, retrieved memory set, ground-truth answer, five sampled responses, Qwen3-235B judge verdict, self-reflections; inference: only the meta-memory plus retrieved fragments
signatures.operation: sample 5 responses with current meta-memory -> judge vs ground truth -> reflect on each -> LLM proposes ADD/DEL/MOD actions per instance -> LLM filters conflicting actions -> Exec applies the set; mini-batch of 50, 5 epochs, start from empty
signatures.conditions: labeled QA training data with a trustworthy judge; frozen generator LLM
signatures.feedback: binary correctness by LLM judge against ground truth
signatures.selection_rule: no measured-utility acceptance of an edit; only an LLM conflict filter; DEL available; no rollback or best-checkpoint rule described
signatures.persistence: meta-memory per fold/training run; checkpoints per step exist (used in analysis)
signatures.later_use: appended to the generation prompt for all test queries; also applied to Full Text and RAG systems
signatures.claimed_effect: average 71.90 vs LightMem 67.50 (Qwen); 69.08 vs 66.17 (Llama); w/o Evolution 68.33
signatures.failure_boundary: accuracy declines after step 5; Single-Assistant category far below RAG/Full Text; judge dependence; in-domain > out-of-domain

gap.author_gap: Memory construction methods yield fragmented or contradictory units that break logical/temporal relations; LLMs are not taught how to use memorized knowledge.
gap.checked_gap: The failure mode is real (qualitative road-trip case; accuracy gains on Multi-Session and Temporal Reasoning), and the fixed object is the reader-side guidance (no learned utilization guidance in prior memory systems). Nearest neighbors cited are construction/storage systems (LightMem, G-Memory, Mem0, A-Mem, MemoryOS); experience/reflection stores and learned memory managers, which also write guidance from outcomes, are not discussed or compared, so the novelty of "meta-memory" relative to them is unchecked.
gap.lineage: RAG/full context -> stateful memory systems (Mem0, A-Mem, MemoryOS) -> consolidation systems (LightMem, G-Memory) -> learned utilization experience (MetaMem)
gap.residue: Whether learned usage guidance beats a hand-written generic usage prompt or other reflective optimizers is untested; category-specific regressions (Single-Assistant) unexplained.
gap.stakes: accuracy on long-horizon multi-session reasoning with scattered evidence
gap.method_response: Self-reflective ADD/DEL/MOD optimization of a meta-memory against ground-truth correctness, applied at inference on top of any memory system.
gap.remaining_gap: No admission/rollback gate, over-training decline after step 5, judge dependence, uncontrolled baseline protocol.
unresolved: comparison to hand-written usage guidance and other reflective optimizers

assessment.strongest_supported_claim: Author-reported: a persisted, LLM-edited meta-memory built from labeled questions raises average LongMemEval accuracy over LightMem by about 4.4 (Qwen) and 2.9 (Llama) points on disjoint test folds, with smaller gains when applied to Full Text/RAG; performance decays with over-training and is worse than RAG/Full Text on Single-Assistant.
not_supported: benefit of the evolving procedure over hand-written generic guidance
assessment.author_vs_our: All numbers author_report; fold means and margins are our arithmetic from the authors tables, not reruns.

G.reason: A real utilization gap (fragmented/contradictory units) with a qualitative case and category gains, but nearest neighbors are only storage/consolidation systems; reflective experience stores and learned memory managers are not checked and the residual is thin.

M.reason: Mechanism is concrete and reconstructible (judge vs ground truth, per-response reflection, ADD/DEL/MOD actions, conflict filter, prompt injection) and makes distinguishable predictions (application to Full Text/RAG, over-training decline, judge insensitivity).

X.reason: Edit vocabulary, batch loop, conflict filtering and next-round reading are explicit, and per-step checkpoints exist, but no edit-level acceptance test, no rollback to the best step, forgetting is left to the LLM, and the final checkpoint rule is unspecified.

E.measurement.reason: Standard benchmark accuracy with LLM-judge scoring, judge model swapped in Table 6, fold table provided; but the Qwen LightMem row is not on the same five folds (67.50 vs fold mean 65.9) and the same judge family drives construction and scoring.

E.causality.reason: w/o Evolution, w/o Self-Reflection and application to Full Text/RAG isolate parts of the mechanism, but the main ablation is under-defined and there is no hand-written-guidance, alternative-optimizer or budget-matched control.

E.holdout.reason: Test questions are disjoint from construction questions in each of five folds and a second corpus (ShareGPT) is used for construction; open points are the unspecified validation/checkpoint rule (peak at step 5) and unaudited base-model contamination.

E.statistics.reason: Fold-level table gives a replication count (9 of 10 wins; one loss) and category sizes are listed, but no CIs, seeds or tests, and per-fold categories hold as few as 6 items.

E.cost.reason: Inference tokens/latency are compared (negligible overhead), but the construction cost (5 samples x judge x reflection x action x filter x 5 epochs) and baselines budgets are not reported.
